title: Fractions on a Number Line
description: Learn fractions on a number line for Class 3: represent and compare fractions, find equivalent fractions. Free online tests and IMO practice.

topics.title: Represent Fractions on a Number Line
topics.concept:
A number line shows fractions between whole numbers. To plot a fraction:

  1. Divide the distance from 0 to 1 into equal parts (number = denominator)
  2. Count that many parts from 0 (number = numerator)

Example: 3/4 → divide into 4 equal parts, count 3 from 0.

examples.solution: Divide 0-to-1 into 4 equal parts. Count 3 steps from 0. Mark the point at 3/4.
Divide into 3 equal parts. 1/3 is the first mark after 0 — one-third of the way to 1.

recap: Denominator = total equal parts between 0 and 1.
Numerator = how many steps to count from 0.
Farther from 0 on number line = larger fraction.

topics.title: Compare Fractions
topics.concept:
Same denominator: bigger numerator = bigger fraction (5/8 > 3/8)

Same numerator: smaller denominator = bigger fraction (1/3 > 1/4, because thirds are bigger than fourths)

examples.solution: Same numerator (1). Smaller denominator = bigger fraction. 3 < 4, so 1/3 > 1/4.

recap: Same bottom number: bigger top = bigger fraction.
Same top number: bigger bottom = smaller fraction.
On number line: fractions closer to 1 are larger.

topics.title: Equivalent Fractions
topics.concept:
Equivalent fractions look different but have the same value.

1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8

To find equivalent fractions: multiply both top and bottom by the same number.

Example: 2/3 x (4/4) = 8/12. So 2/3 = 8/12.

examples.problem: Find a fraction equivalent to 2/3 with denominator 6.
examples.solution: Multiply top and bottom by 2: (2x2)/(3x2) = 4/6. So 2/3 = 4/6.
3/4 x (2/2) = 6/8. Yes, they are equivalent fractions.

recap: Equivalent fractions = same amount, different notation.
Multiply both numerator and denominator by the same number.

questions.q: On a number line from 0 to 1 divided into 5 equal parts, where is 3/5?
questions.explanation: 3/5 = 3 steps out of 5. It sits at the 3rd mark from 0.
Same numerator (1). Smaller denominator = bigger fraction. 2 < 3, so 1/2 > 1/3.

questions.q: On a number line, which fraction is closer to 1: 2/3 or 4/5?
A pizza is cut into 8 slices. You eat 3 slices. Your friend eats 1/4 of the pizza. Who ate more?
questions.explanation: You ate 3/8. Friend ate 1/4 = 2/8. 3/8 > 2/8, so you ate more.
If numerator x4: 2x4=8. So denominator x4: 3x4=12. Answer: 8/12.

questions.q: Which fraction is exactly halfway between 1/4 and 3/4?
questions.explanation: Halfway between 1/4 and 3/4 = (1/4 + 3/4)/2 = (4/4)/2 = 1/2. And 2/4 = 1/2. So both B and C are correct.

questions.q: Is 3/4 equivalent to 9/12? Show by multiplying.
questions.explanation: 3/4 x (3/3) = 9/12. Yes, they are equivalent because multiplying top and bottom by 3 gives 9/12.
